newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: U.S. says opposed to using force in Spratlys row.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says opposed to using force in Spratlys row.

text.p: The U.S. ambassador to the Philippines said on Thursday that Washington would oppose any use of force to resolve disputes over ownership of islands in the South China Sea.

Ambassador Thomas Hubbard, talking to reporters, urged rival claimants to the Spratly Islands and adjacent islets, reefs and shoals to solve their quarrel by peaceful means. The islands have no apparent commercial value but some analysts believe they could lie atop large reserves of crude oil and natural gas.

A long-standing row between the Philippines and China over the Spratlys and a rocky outcrop called Scarborough Shoal has intensified after Manila last week arrested 21 Chinese fishermen for allegedly poaching near the shoal. China has demanded the release of the fishermen, saying they were in Chinese waters. "We would strongly oppose any effort to solve this problem by using force and we made known to all parties of the region that we encourage their efforts to solve the problem and we're happy to help them do that," Hubbard said.
